title: Cause-and-Effect Chain
description: Trace a printer that jams every afternoon back through four intermediate causes to its root cause.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Foundations of Systems Thinking

educational.learningObjective: Given a chain of events, the learner will trace each cause to its effect and identify which link in the chain is the root cause versus a surface-level symptom.
prerequisites: Can distinguish a cause from an effect
Has encountered a recurring problem that was "fixed" more than once
learningOutcomes: Trace a multi-step causal chain from symptom back to root cause
Distinguish a root cause from an intermediate cause and from a symptom
Explain why treating a symptom lets the problem recur
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a different symptom and ask them to propose a three-link chain ending in a root cause. Check that the proposed root cause is something that could actually be changed.

pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Five Whys reasoning made visible one link at a time
pedagogical.feedbackType: An explanation panel naming the causal mechanism for each link
misconceptionsAddressed: That the most visible cause is the root cause
That fixing the last link in a chain prevents recurrence
discussionQuestions: Why do organizations keep fixing symptoms even when the root cause is known?
How many "whys" is enough before you have reached a root cause?
Can a chain have more than one root cause? What would that look like?
